name: Rudy Giuliani
role: Mayor of New York City (1994-2001); US Associate Attorney General; 2008 Republican presidential candidate; lawyer to Donald Trump (2018-2021)
summary: A former prosecutor and New York mayor who ran a tough-on-crime, tax-cutting, pro-market city government while holding socially liberal views on abortion, gay rights and immigration. As a 2008 presidential candidate he stressed a forceful anti-terror and pro-military foreign policy, school vouchers, health savings accounts and free trade; since 2016 he has been a prominent Trump ally.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Rejected government-run or mandated universal coverage as 'socialized medicine' (Apr and Dec 2007); proposed tax deductions, health savings accounts and vouchers for poor people instead, saying government 'has never been able to reduce costs'.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Only a conditional remark in his 2000 Senate race (support an increase if studies showed no job losses) was found; not a position on a substantial raise.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Said 'the free market is one of our greatest assets' and that 'free-market principles are the only things that reduce cost and improve quality'; ran as a supply-side tax cutter.

public-ownership.rationale: No statement or record from Giuliani that addresses this was found in the sources reviewed.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Opposed raising the capital-gains rate (rejecting Edwards's 15% to 28% idea), said letting the Bush tax cuts expire would hurt the economy, wanted the Bush tax cuts made permanent, the death tax eliminated 'immediately' and the capital-gains and corporate rates cut. Said new tax increases are a 'liberal Democratic assumption'.

unions-good.rationale: Mixed: said unions 'have made a positive contribution' and credited a vibrant union for the UAW pact, but also said 'there are good unions and bad unions' and attacked the school unions as holding children back.

property-fundamental.rationale: Listed 'protections for private property' with low taxes, sensible regulation and free trade as the model that brings national wealth; not stated as a near-absolute right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Wanted regulations kept 'moderate' and promised to review them 'so that America doesn't over regulate businesses'; said business leaves when government over-regulates and over-taxes.

cut-welfare.rationale: Moved roughly 600,000 people off New York City welfare through workfare, and his campaign material described welfare dependency as a problem to be replaced by work; also proposed a 10% cut in non-military federal spending.

worker-ownership.rationale: No statement or record from Giuliani that addresses this was found in the sources reviewed.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Wrote that the next president must 'preserve the gains made by the USA Patriot Act and not unrealistically limit electronic surveillance'; said the president 'must be free to defend the nation' and urged keeping electronic surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Called the push for medical marijuana 'really a way to legalize it' and said 'there's no reason for it'; he said marijuana 'adds nothing' to the legal medications available. Opposition to legalizing other drugs is not documented, so this rests on marijuana.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: No statement or record from Giuliani that addresses this was found in the sources reviewed.

strong-leader.rationale: No statement or record from Giuliani that addresses this was found in the sources reviewed.

state-harmful.rationale: No recorded position on this statement: drawn from how he ran government and expanded police, not a stated view on whether the state is harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Mixed: as mayor he backed written tests and licensing for gun owners, the federal assault-weapons ban and sued gun makers, but as a 2007 candidate said the Second Amendment is an individual right and only 'reasonable' regulation, mostly state by state, is allowed.

empower-police-military.rationale: Wrote that the Army needs at least ten new combat brigades and that the 'peace dividend' left the military too small; as mayor built up the NYPD, defended police after the Diallo verdict and backed aggressive enforcement.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No statement or record from Giuliani that addresses this was found in the sources reviewed.

decide-locally.rationale: Repeatedly said abortion funding, Roe, campus gun rules and gun regulation should be decided state by state in 'a federal system', though he also backed federal licensing and federal immigration controls.

rehabilitation.rationale: No statement or record from Giuliani that addresses this was found in the sources reviewed.

traditional-family.rationale: No statement or record from Giuliani that addresses this was found in the sources reviewed.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In June 2015 told Fox News 'I'm in favor of gay rights, I'm in favor of gay marriage. I see it as an issue of equality'; earlier (2007, 2011) he had opposed it. Most recent position counts.

abortion-legal.rationale: Describes himself as personally against abortion but pro-choice: 'ultimately a woman should make that [decision] with her conscience and her doctor'; would not criminalize it, though he backs parental consent with bypass and the partial-birth ban.

more-religion-public.rationale: Mixed: opposes school prayer but defended a teacher fired for praying with students and said the Ten Commandments are 'part of Western civilization'.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Said he was 'very uncomfortable' with Tancredo's call to halt legal immigration and that the debate should be about illegal immigration, which he wants stopped at the border; also warned that failing to end illegal immigration risks legal immigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Wrote that the UN 'has proved irrelevant to the resolution of almost every major dispute' and is 'weak, indecisive, and outright corrupt', and that 'we should not expect much more of it'.

free-trade.rationale: Wrote 'ever more open trade throughout the world is essential'; said NAFTA has been good and urged passing the Peru, Colombia, Panama and South Korea deals rather than 'turn our back on free trade'.

nation-first.rationale: Mixed: wrote that the realist doctrine 'defines America's interests too narrowly' and urged strengthening the international system, while distrusting the UN and stressing American interests.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Defended removing Saddam partly because he 'slaughtered' his own people and abused women, and said the world's commitment to end genocide in Darfur was 'sidestepped again and again'; also wrote that human rights must be a core commitment.

open-borders.rationale: Called for stopping illegal immigration 'right at the border' with a physical and virtual fence, more Border Patrol and a tamper-proof ID so no one enters without identifying themselves.

limit-growth.rationale: Ran on 'growth principles'; rejected carbon taxes and mandates and preferring new technology and energy independence to limits on activity.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Accepted that humans contribute to warming but opposed Kyoto, a carbon tax and a mandated 35 mpg standard, favouring an Apollo-style push on alternative energy and energy independence instead.
